scope: Proposition 4.5 (Uniform area transfer) of the manuscript “The Penrose inequality for maximal asymptotically hyperbolic initial data” (preprints/The-Penrose-inequality-for-maximal-asymptotically-hyperbolic-initial-data-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 641d4aa3892adbca), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the capped topology (X, O), a number A∗ > 0, and a scalar lower bound CR ≥ 0. Suppose a comparison has the following properties. (i) The smooth complete metric ˆ︁ h has one AH or AF end with the mean-curvature and radial- gradient asymptotics used in (4.4). The cap-only enclosure E0 is a smooth precompact strictly outward-minimizing set, with minimal boundary disjoint from O, every component meeting O, and Scalˆ︁ h ≥ −CR outside E0. (ii) On X \O there are a reference metric gbase, positive functions x, W, a metric ḡ, and a weight 0 < ρ ≤ 1, such that ḡ ≥ gbase, dVḡ = W dVgbase , (1 − η)xḡ ≤ ˆ︁ h ≤ (1 + η)xḡ. (4.18) (iii) Every enclosing C1 surface with connected exterior, as in Lemma 4.4, satisfies ∫︂ N ρ dAgbase ≥ (1 − q)A∗. (4.19) In the piecewise case this is required for surfaces having zero area in the joining surface. For every 0 < ε < 1 there are positive tolerances η0, q0, δ0 and v0, depending only on ε, A∗, CR and the integer b2 in (4.1), with the following consequence. If η ≤ η0, q ≤ q0, 0 < δ ≤ δ0, and ∫︂ {x<1−δ} ρ3/2 W dVgbase < v0, (4.20) then |∂E0|ˆ︁ h ≥ (1 − ε)A∗. (4.21) The tolerances are uniform over all comparisons satisfying these conditions; the geometry and initial area of E0 may vary.
